confirmed.title: Craigslist: on a 3-photo listing, 'Image 3' shows photo 1 in Sift while the original shows photo 3
confirmed.where: Craigslist listing page, image buttons under the photo (src/content/extract/generic.ts figureImage, the 'framed' slide test near line 6333)
confirmed.evidence: Listing https://www.craigslist.org/view/d/novato-fuji-adventurer-mountain-bike/9BHB9U3Ac3WQ3XfVJsKrpw has 3 photos (#thumbs 3, Sift shows Image 1-3). After clicking 'Image 3' (3 tries, waits of 3-5 s), Sift's main img src is 00t0t… (photo 1) and its alt ends in '… Needs Repair 1'. 'Image 3' still gets aria-pressed=true. The original's .swipe box is at left 159, width 600. Its slides sit at 759 (photo 1), -441 (photo 2) and 159 (photo 3), so the original shows photo 3. Image 1 and Image 2 show the right photo (Image 2: src 00N0N…, slide 2 at 159). Shot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-4/research/shots/r14t4-cl-img3.png ('Image 3' pressed, photo 1 shown). On a 5-photo listing (/view/d/los-gatos-2005-specialized-rockhopper/ao92DvgK9PFs4S6XFgbZuL), Image 3, 4, 5 and 1 all matched the original. Round 12 checked a 10-photo listing, so I cannot call this a regression.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=<port> SIFT_TAB=<tab> bun scripts/act.ts goto:<any Craigslist listing with exactly 3 photos> wait:8000 'click:Image 3' wait:3000 "eval:[document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelector('main img').src.split('/').pop(), [...document.querySelectorAll('.slide')].map(s=>Math.round(s.getBoundingClientRect().left)+':'+s.querySelector('img').src.split('/').pop())]" prints Sift's img as photo 1, and the slide at the .swipe left edge (159) is photo 3.
confirmed.suspectedCause: figureImage keeps the slides that intersect the figure element's box and picks the first one. In this 3-slide layout, photo 1 waits as the 'next' slide at left 759, the right edge of the 600 px .swipe box. It still counts as framed (the figure's box is wider than .swipe, or the edge test includes it) and comes first in DOM order. Testing against the clipping slider box (.swipe, overflow hidden), or preferring the slide whose left equals the box's left, would pick photo 3.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, high. I reproduced it on 2 loads of the same 3-photo listing. After 'Image 3', Sift shows 00t0t (photo 1, alt '... Needs Repair 1'), and 'Image 3' has aria-pressed=true. The original's slides sit at 759 (00t0t), -441 (00N0N) and 159 (00c0c). With Sift switched off, elementFromPoint in the .swipe box returns 00c0c, and the original reads 'image 3 of 3' (shots: research/shots/skeptic-cl-sift.png and skeptic-cl-orig.png). Image 2 is correct. The cause is exact. figure.iw spans 159..761, but .swipe (overflow hidden) spans 159..759. Slide 1, at 759..1359, passes the framed test because 759 < fr.right - 1 = 760. It then ties slide 3 on width (600) and wins on DOM order, since the width loop only takes a wider image (w > bestW). main's figureImage (generic.ts:6329) is identical, so main has the bug too.
confirmed.fix: src/content/extract/generic.ts figureImage (about line 6333-6349). Rank framed images by how much of their area is visible inside the figure's box (or inside the nearest clipping ancestor with overflow hidden, here .swipe), not by width with DOM order breaking ties. Or count an image as framed only if at least half its width is inside the box. A 2 px sliver of the next slide must not win.

confirmed.suspectedCause: The in-page jump (scroll and/or the page's own JS scroll) triggers the mutation, scroll or hash re-look path, and each look of a 677-comment thread costs 500-670 ms. Skipping or cheapening re-looks after an in-page jump that changes no DOM (or one reused look) would bring it near the original.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium. I ran my own script without the profiler on 2 loads of item 50224463 (677 comments), at light load. Sift's 'next' moved focus to the right comment (fwlr, then AnotherGoodName, at y=74) at 1398, 1399 and 1220 ms. Each click caused three long tasks: 609/551/467, 519/694/623 and 607/461/593 ms. With Sift off in the same tab, the original fired scroll events from 28-36 ms and had no long tasks. One caveat the claim leaves out: the original's smooth scroll reaches the target only at about 1519 ms. So arrival time is about equal. The real harm is 1.2-1.4 s with no feedback after a click while the page is frozen, plus another ~600 ms freeze after focus lands. The cause is in the code. The link path in index.ts (about line 3485) calls afterAct(), which schedules 3 full looks at 60, 400 and 1200 ms (line ~3195). The host click listener (line 2733) adds another look. One look of this thread costs 400-750 ms (the extractor harness gave the same cost for this copy and for main). followAnchor's showPlace (150 ms timer) waits behind those looks. main's index.ts is identical.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts. In the link click path (about line 3485), when the link is a same-page anchor (followAnchor applies), run showPlace before any re-look. In afterAct (about line 3192), skip the fixed 60/400/1200 ms looks unless the page actually mutated (let the MutationObserver drive them), or make it one look. The host click listener at line 2733 should not add a second look on the same click.

confirmed.suspectedCause: An inference from a focus trace and the code, not proven. The page's name.focus() during the replayed click fires sift-focus, which schedules followPageFocus with setTimeout(0). Later in the visit, the re-render for the page change has not run by then. So followPageFocus finds Sift's existing Rename <button> with the same data-ref, sees it already focused, and clears pageFocusTo. The next render turns that ref into a textarea. Preact reuses the old <button> node for the following control (Invite people), and focus stays on it. During boot the render runs first, so the follow finds the textarea. Lead: keep pageFocusTo for the next render when the matched control is not an editable field but the page element is now editable (contenteditable/input), or key controls by ref so a node is never reused for another control.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on both fixtures, fx/r11int-focusclose.html and fx/r12int-focusportal.html, with my own script (scratchpad/skeptic-n0/rn.ts). Mouse click on Sift's 'Rename list: Groceries' 5 s after load, then typing ' and bread' and Tab: log ['editing','share open'], name 'Groceries', share box open. This failed in 3 of 3 runs on focusclose and 2 of 2 on focusportal. It also failed with a 3.5 s load wait. Keyboard (focus Rename, Enter, type XY, Tab) failed 2 of 2 on focusclose and 1 of 1 on focusportal. Sift's focus sits on 'Invite people', the log stays ['editing'], the name stays 'Groceries', and the page is left in editing. At 1.5 s and 2.5 s the text does reach the name. The original (Alt+Shift+S, click #name, same typing) gives ['editing','edit ended: Groceries and bread'] in 3 of 3 runs, so the difference comes from Sift, not the page. One part of the suspected cause is wrong. Preact does not reuse the node. My probe shows the focused Rename button [data-ref r8] is removed (isConnected false). Sift renders a textarea [data-ref r8] for the name. Focus then lands on a different node, the 'Invite people' button [ra]. Sift's window-capture focusin listener swallows that focusin. The move comes from paint() calling refocus(). twinOf() wants the same tag, so the textarea with the same ref does not count. The first 'near' control wins, which is 'Invite people'. The rest of the suspected cause matches the code. The setTimeout(0) followPageFocus already ran against the old Rename button. That button was focused, so it cleared pageFocusTo, and the followPageFocus() call after paint does nothing. In the early runs the trace shows the same jump to 'Invite people', and then followPageFocus moves focus on to the textarea. Unclaimed side note: even when it works (1.5 s, 2.5 s), the typed text lands at the start ('edit ended:  and breadGroceries'). The original gives 'Groceries and bread'.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts twinOf() (~311): when spot.ref is set, accept the control with the same data-ref even if its tag changed, at least a button that became an input or textarea. Then refocus keeps focus on the same page element instead of falling through to spot.near. Also, followPageFocus() (~3396) should not clear pageFocusTo when the matched ctl is not an editable field but to.el now is (isContentEditable or input/textarea). Keep it for the call after paint(). When following into a textarea that stands for a contenteditable, put the caret where the page's selection is, or at the end, so typing appends as on the original.

skeptic.verdict: Partly fixed, confirmed at medium severity. I measured on Chrome 9466, tab skeptic, with firstpaint.ts h1. The machine was heavily loaded (load average 13 to 23 on 6 cores), so absolute times are inflated. The gap Sift adds was steady, though. core-buttons3000: original 312 vs Sift 612 ms (5 runs per side), then 380 vs 746 ms (3 runs). That is +300 to +366 ms. core-buttonsli3000: 202 vs 639 ms (+437), then 452 vs 756 ms (+304). core-nav3000: 269 vs 546 ms (+277). core-buttons1000: 272 vs 577 ms (+305). So Sift is still 1.7 to 3.2x later, adding about 0.3 to 0.45 s. Round 13's target was within about 100 ms. My core-budget run gave 242 vs 614 ms (+372). That is worse than the claim's 323 vs 364, but it is one 3-run set under load, so I do not dispute the claim's 'fixed' there. Sift on delayed DOMContentLoaded to 3.0 to 9.1 s on core-budget, against 1.0 to 1.6 s off. In one logged load, the full look after the partial view was a single 10.4 s long task (data-ms 9207). So the freeze after first content is real. Cause, from a trace and CPU profile of core-buttons3000 with Sift on: one long task of 343 to 437 ms comes right before Sift's first content. Almost all of it is Sift's own code: DOMContentLoaded handler, then loadedAgain, then run, then extract at 253 ms; paint is only 24 ms. A per-look log shows the look before DOMContentLoaded rendered only the 'Loading' line. The budgeted first look (50 ms budget) then took 210 to 317 ms and showed the list's first part (908 chars). A full look of 737 to 1023 ms followed. The 50 ms budget overruns 4 to 6x. pastDeadline() in extract/generic.ts is checked only inside the walk, after 256 elements. mainRoot, besideMain, mainCompanions, visibleMains, tlen and detectItems/controlInto all run over the whole page or the whole 3000-child grid with no deadline. These are not artifacts: Sift off has no such task, and the fixtures have no page scripts.
skeptic.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts, make the first-look deadline cover more than the walk. Inside detectItems/controlInto, while a deadline is set, examine only the first screenful of a container's children. Bound the whole-page scans in mainRoot, besideMain, mainCompanions and visibleMains (tlen over every element), for example by checking pastDeadline or capping the scanned elements while deadline < Infinity. In src/content/index.ts run(), the first look before DOMContentLoaded rendered only the Loading line; the content was not shown until the next look, after DOMContentLoaded. Either let that look (budget 50) render the partial content it reads, or bring the next one forward. For core-budget's after-first-view freeze, the full look (budget 0) should be split across tasks or kept away from the DOMContentLoaded task. loadedAgain currently runs it synchronously there, which freezes the view for seconds.

skeptic.verdict: Partly fixed, confirmed at medium severity. I measured on Chrome 9466, tab skeptic, with firstpaint.ts h1. The machine was heavily loaded (load average 13 to 23 on 6 cores), so absolute times are inflated. The gap Sift adds was steady, though. core-buttons3000: original 312 vs Sift 612 ms (5 runs per side), then 380 vs 746 ms (3 runs). That is +300 to +366 ms. core-buttonsli3000: 202 vs 639 ms (+437), then 452 vs 756 ms (+304). core-nav3000: 269 vs 546 ms (+277). core-buttons1000: 272 vs 577 ms (+305). So Sift is still 1.7 to 3.2x later, adding about 0.3 to 0.45 s. Round 13's target was within about 100 ms. My core-budget run gave 242 vs 614 ms (+372). That is worse than the claim's 323 vs 364, but it is one 3-run set under load, so I do not dispute the claim's 'fixed' there. Sift on delayed DOMContentLoaded to 3.0 to 9.1 s on core-budget, against 1.0 to 1.6 s off. In one logged load, the full look after the partial view was a single 10.4 s long task (data-ms 9207). So the freeze after first content is real. Cause, from a trace and CPU profile of core-buttons3000 with Sift on: one long task of 343 to 437 ms comes right before Sift's first content. Almost all of it is Sift's own code: DOMContentLoaded handler, then loadedAgain, then run, then extract at 253 ms; paint is only 24 ms. A per-look log shows the look before DOMContentLoaded rendered only the 'Loading' line. The budgeted first look (50 ms budget) then took 210 to 317 ms and showed the list's first part (908 chars). A full look of 737 to 1023 ms followed. The 50 ms budget overruns 4 to 6x. pastDeadline() in extract/generic.ts is checked only inside the walk, after 256 elements. mainRoot, besideMain, mainCompanions, visibleMains, tlen and detectItems/controlInto all run over the whole page or the whole 3000-child grid with no deadline. These are not artifacts: Sift off has no such task, and the fixtures have no page scripts.
skeptic.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts, make the first-look deadline cover more than the walk. Inside detectItems/controlInto, while a deadline is set, examine only the first screenful of a container's children. Bound the whole-page scans in mainRoot, besideMain, mainCompanions and visibleMains (tlen over every element), for example by checking pastDeadline or capping the scanned elements while deadline < Infinity. In src/content/index.ts run(), the first look before DOMContentLoaded rendered only the Loading line; the content was not shown until the next look, after DOMContentLoaded. Either let that look (budget 50) render the partial content it reads, or bring the next one forward. For core-budget's after-first-view freeze, the full look (budget 0) should be split across tasks or kept away from the DOMContentLoaded task. loadedAgain currently runs it synchronously there, which freezes the view for seconds.
